list.title: Web forms
list.empty_body_admin: A web form is a page you embed on your own site. What people fill in becomes a lead here, with no login and no copy-pasting.
list.empty_body_member: Nobody has built a web form for this organisation yet. An admin can create one.
list.unpublish_explain: Stops accepting submissions. The embed stays on the site and starts refusing people.
list.delete_explain: Removes the form and its submission history. Leads already created stay.
list.truncated_after: . The rest are reachable through the API.
list.footer_heading: A published form accepts posts from anyone
list.footer_body: It has to: the whole point is that a stranger can fill it in without an account. A honeypot field, per-form and per-address rate limits, and disposable-address rejection are always on, and each form can add a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge of its own. Publish only the forms you are embedding, and unpublish one the moment you take its snippet off your site.
list.err_create_forbidden: Only an admin can create a web form. A form accepts leads from anyone on the internet, so making one is an admin action.
list.err_publish_forbidden: Only an admin can publish a web form.
list.err_unpublish_forbidden: Only an admin can unpublish a web form.
list.err_delete_forbidden: Only an admin can remove a web form.

detail.state_published_sub: Accepting submissions from anyone with the embed.
detail.state_draft_sub: Collecting nothing until it is published.
detail.unpublish_explain: The embed stays on the site and starts refusing people.
detail.publish_blocker_no_fields: Add at least one field first.
detail.publish_blocker_no_email: Add an email field before publishing. It is what lets a repeat submission update the existing lead instead of failing.
detail.publish_blocker_incomplete: Every field needs a label and something to write into.
detail.publish_blocker_no_redirect: This form redirects on success but has no redirect URL set.
detail.section_fields_sub: What a visitor is asked, in the order they are asked it. An email field is required before the form can be published.
detail.no_fields: No fields yet. A form with no fields collects nothing.
detail.section_behaviour_sub: What the visitor sees after they submit, and where the lead lands.
detail.name: Name
detail.name_hint: Internal only. The visitor never sees it.
detail.redirect_url_hint: http or https only. The embed navigates the visitor's browser here, so any other scheme would be a script running on your own site.
detail.lead_source_hint: Which form a lead came from is recorded separately, so this can stay broad.
detail.notify_profiles: Email these people on each lead
detail.notify_profiles_hint: Nobody selected means no notification is sent.
detail.section_spam_sub: A hidden honeypot field, a per-address rate limit and a per-form one are always on and are not configurable. These are the parts you choose.
detail.allowed_origins_hint_1: One per line, scheme and host only, no path. Leave empty and the iframe embed works anywhere.
detail.allowed_origins_hint_strong: The script embed needs the site's origin listed here
detail.allowed_origins_hint_2: : the browser refuses a cross-origin POST that we have not permitted, and a form with no listed origins permits none.
detail.captcha_secret_ph_stored: Stored. Leave blank to keep it.
detail.captcha_secret_hint: Never shown again once saved; we only send it to Cloudflare. Leaving this blank keeps whatever is stored rather than clearing it.
detail.captcha_secret_hint_strong: No secret is stored yet. Verification fails closed, so publishing with Turnstile on and no secret would refuse every submission.
detail.section_embed_sub: Paste one of these into your own site. Both are built by the server, because they need this API's address and a browser only knows your site's.
detail.embed_iframe_note: Works anywhere, no origin list needed.
detail.embed_script_warn: This one will not work yet. Add the site's origin under Spam first: the browser blocks a cross-origin POST unless we permit that origin, and this form permits none.
detail.section_activity_sub: The last 30 days. A view is counted when the embed loads, whether or not anyone fills it in.
detail.activity_empty: Nothing submitted yet. Rejected attempts would be listed here too, so an empty list means nobody has reached the form at all.
detail.delete_body: Removes the form and its submission history. Leads it already created stay where they are. Any embed still on your site will stop working.
detail.err_save_forbidden: Only an admin can change a web form.
detail.err_publish_forbidden: Only an admin can publish a web form.
detail.err_unpublish_forbidden: Only an admin can unpublish a web form.
detail.err_delete_forbidden: Only an admin can remove a web form.
detail.err_not_found: That web form does not exist.

custom_fields.label: Label

custom_fields.key_hint_existing: Fixed after creation. Every value already stored is filed under this key, and changing it would leave them all behind.
custom_fields.field_type_hint_existing: Fixed after creation. Values already stored were written and checked against this type.
custom_fields.choices_hint: Renaming a choice keeps the values already stored against it. Removing one leaves the records that hold it showing a value the list no longer offers.
custom_fields.required_hint: Binds new writes only. Records saved before this keep their gap.
custom_fields.filterable_hint: Can be used to narrow a list, not just read on the record.

custom_fields.gap_tail: . Marking a field required binds new writes only, nothing goes back and fills in what was saved before.
custom_fields.turn_off_explain: Stops being collected. Stored values stay.
custom_fields.footer_note: A field marked with the filter icon can be used to narrow a list; the rest are readable only on the record itself. Turning a field off stops it being collected and hides it, and leaves the values already stored on each record untouched.

api_tokens.forbidden_text: Reviewing every token in the organization is limited to admins, because a token authenticates as its owner. Ask an admin if one needs issuing or revoking.
api_tokens.created_body: This is the only time the full token is shown. Store it somewhere safe; it cannot be retrieved again.
api_tokens.revoked_orphaned_result: {count, plural, one {Revoked # token on deactivated accounts.} other {Revoked # tokens on deactivated accounts.}}
api_tokens.loose_end_text: {count, plural, one {# live token belongs to a deactivated account.} other {# live tokens belong to a deactivated account.}} Deactivating already stops them at login, but they are not revoked. Reactivating the account would bring them back.
api_tokens.revoke_orphaned_button: {count, plural, one {Revoke it} other {Revoke them all}}
api_tokens.footer_heading: A token is the whole account
api_tokens.footer_body: A token authenticates as its owner and inherits their role and organisation. There is no narrower permission to give it. Issue one per integration so a single revocation stops a single thing, set an expiry, and revoke anything you cannot name a use for. The value is shown once when the token is created and cannot be recovered afterwards.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.sub_all: One policy per priority · all four are configured
escalation.priority_fixed_hint: Fixed after creation. One policy per priority.
escalation.fr_hours_hint: How long a ticket at this priority may wait for its first reply, counted in business hours. Leave blank to use the built-in {hours}.
escalation.res_hours_hint: Applies to tickets opened from now on, and to any ticket moved to this priority. Tickets already open keep the target they were given.
escalation.target_inactive_hint: This target's account is no longer active. It stays set until you change it, and a breach sent there waits for someone who cannot sign in.
escalation.no_target_hint: Nothing happens on this half until a target is picked. A team on its own is not notified.
escalation.reassign_hint: Reassigns the ticket. No email is sent, to them or to the team.
escalation.no_teams: No teams in this org yet.
escalation.active_help: Starts escalating breaches at this priority as soon as it is saved.
escalation.empty_body: An escalation policy decides what happens when a ticket misses its first-response or resolution target. One per priority. None are set for this organisation, so a breach currently escalates to nobody.
escalation.unheard_heading: {count, plural, one {breach in the last 30 days told nobody} other {breaches in the last 30 days told nobody}}
escalation.unheard_body_some: Some halves of these policies resolve to no recipient.
escalation.unheard_body_dead: {dead} of {total} policies do nothing at all when a ticket breaches.
escalation.unheard_body_tail: A policy that exists is not the same as a policy that fires.
escalation.deactivate_explain: Stops escalating breaches at this priority. It stays in the list, off, until turned back on.
escalation.remove_explain: Deleted permanently. Breaches at this priority will escalate to nobody.
escalation.team_ignored: {team} is not notified here: this half only reassigns.
escalation.outcome_off: Nothing. The policy is turned off
escalation.outcome_no_target_team: Nothing. No target is set, and {team} is not notified on its own
escalation.unconfigured_note: {count, plural, one {{list} has no policy, so breaches at that priority escalate to nobody and are not counted above.} other {{list} have no policy, so breaches at those priorities escalate to nobody and are not counted above.}}
escalation.footer_after: , so a breach counts working time only, and time spent waiting on the customer does not count at all. Editing a policy sets both the target and who hears about a breach.

escalation.error_deactivate_fallback: Could not turn the policy off.

reopen.stat_missed_detail_off: Not counted while reopening is off

business_hours.title: Business hours
business_hours.sub_always_on: no day open, so targets run around the clock
business_hours.always_on_heading: Every day is closed, and the clock still runs
business_hours.always_on_body: A four-hour target expires four hours after the ticket arrives, weekend or not. The engine drops a calendar that never opens rather than treating it as permanently shut, so open at least one day to make this calendar count.
business_hours.default_note: This is the default calendar, so it applies to every ticket that does not have a more specific one.
business_hours.holiday_dup_before: That date was already a holiday, called
business_hours.holiday_dup_after: . The name you typed was not saved: remove it and add it again to rename it.
business_hours.remove_holiday_explain: Deletes it. The day counts as working time again.
business_hours.holidays_empty: No holidays set. Targets will keep running on public holidays.
business_hours.effect_always_on: With no day open, targets do not count anything out: they run on the wall clock, through evenings, weekends and the holidays below.
business_hours.effect_before: Response and resolution targets count only the time inside these hours. A ticket opened at 17:20 on Friday
business_hours.effect_starts_next: starts its clock whenever the week next opens,
business_hours.effect_after: so the weekend does not spend a four-hour target.
business_hours.error_forbidden: Only admins can update business hours.

inbound_email.title: Inbound email
inbound_email.address_hint: Mail to the old address stops becoming tickets.
inbound_email.provider_hint: Only AWS SES is implemented. The other three are stored and accepted, and mail sent to an address using one becomes nothing until that integration exists.
inbound_email.assignee_inactive_hint: This assignee's account is no longer active. It stays set until you change it, so new tickets from this address land on someone who cannot sign in.
inbound_email.active_help: Starts creating tickets from mail to this address as soon as it is saved.
inbound_email.silent_heading: {count, plural, one {{addresses} is switched on and creates nothing} other {{addresses} are switched on and create nothing}}
inbound_email.silent_body: Mail keeps arriving and nothing bounces, so anyone writing there gets no ticket and no error, just silence. Each address says below what is stopping it.
inbound_email.tickets_in_30: {count, plural, one {ticket in 30 days} other {tickets in 30 days}}
inbound_email.deactivate_explain: Stops opening tickets from this address. It stays in the list, off, until turned back on.
inbound_email.remove_explain: Deleted permanently. Mail to this address stops becoming tickets, and the signing secret is destroyed.
inbound_email.proof_heading: How a delivery is proved genuine
inbound_email.proof_body1: Two checks, and mail has to clear both: AWS signs each notification, and the address has to be pinned to the exact SNS topic it was subscribed to. The signature alone proves only that some AWS account sent it, so without the pin anyone who learned an address's id could have AWS sign forged mail into this organisation. The pin is set from the first confirmed subscription and is never shown here, because it carries the AWS account id.
inbound_email.proof_body2: There is also a signing-secret field on each address, reserved for providers that sign deliveries that way. None of those are implemented, so nothing compares it today. It can be set through the API and is never readable back, here or anywhere.
inbound_email.footer_before: Where a new ticket goes after it is created is decided by

delivery_why.off: Mail still arrives here and no ticket is opened. Nothing bounces, so whoever wrote gets silence rather than an error.
delivery_why.unsupported: {provider} deliveries are not implemented. The webhook refuses them, so mail to this address becomes nothing whatever else is set here. Only AWS SES is wired up.
delivery_why.unconfirmed: Waiting on the first confirmed delivery from SNS. Until the topic subscription is confirmed, every notification is rejected, so this address is not receiving yet.

inbound_email.error_forbidden: Only an admin can change inbound mailboxes.
inbound_email.error_deactivate_fallback: Could not turn the address off.
inbound_email.error_activate_fallback: Could not turn the address on.
